reason: The hypothesis directly restates the exact sequence of events reported in P1, P6, P11, and P23 for a very similar alloy system: a supersaturated BCC solid solution decomposes upon annealing via elemental segregation, leading to elastic stresses that cause hardening, followed by nucleation of σ and B2 phases. The proposed intervention, mechanism, predicted outcome, and falsification test are all taken from these passages without substantive new elements or integration of disparate findings.
copied_elements: BCC supersaturated solid solution decomposes upon annealing
Element segregation (Mo, Cr, Al) increases during annealing
Elastic stresses build up due to segregation and cause hardening
Secondary phases (σ, B2) nucleate after critical stress/segregation
Annealing at 600–900 °C leads to phase decomposition
Rapid quenching retains single-phase BCC as baseline
XRD, SEM, EDS, microhardness as characterization methods
Falsification by absence of segregation, strain, or secondary phases
